'''Peter Henry George Aczel''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|k|s|əl}}; 31 October 1941  – 1 August 2023) was a British mathematician, logician and [[Emeritus]] joint [[Professor]] in the [[Department of Computer Science, University of Manchester|Department of Computer Science]] and the [[School of Mathematics, University of Manchester|School of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|59287}}</ref> He is known for his work in [[non-well-founded set theory]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/sum2018/entries/nonwellfounded-set-theory/|title=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|first=Lawrence S.|last=Moss|chapter=Non-wellfounded Set Theory |editor-first=Edward N.|editor-last=Zalta|date=February 20, 2018|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|via=Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy}}</ref> [[constructive set theory]],<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Aczel | first1 = P. | author-link = Peter Aczel| chapter = An Introduction to Inductive Definitions | doi = 10.1016/S0049-237X(08)71120-0 | title = Handbook of Mathematical Logic | series = Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics | volume = 90 | pages = 739–201 | year = 1977 | isbn = 9780444863881 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Aczel | first1 = P. | author-link = Peter Aczel| last2 = Mendler | first2 = N. | chapter = A final coalgebra theorem | doi = 10.1007/BFb0018361 | title = Category Theory and Computer Science | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science | volume = 389 | pages = 357 | year = 1989 | isbn = 3-540-51662-X }}</ref> and [[Gottlob Frege|Frege]] structures.<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Aczel | first1 = P.| author-link = Peter Aczel | chapter = Frege Structures and the Notions of Proposition, Truth and Set | doi = 10.1016/S0049-237X(08)71252-7 | title = The Kleene Symposium | series = Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics | volume = 101 | pages = 31–32 | year = 1980 | isbn = 9780444853455 }}</ref><ref name="dblp">{{DBLP|name=Peter Aczel}}</ref>

==Education==
Aczel completed his [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[Mathematics]] in 1963<ref name="peter.aczel">{{Cite web|url=http://www.manchester.ac.uk/research/Peter.Aczel/|title=Peter Aczel page the University of Manchester}}</ref> followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] at the [[University of Oxford]] in 1966 under the supervision of [[John Crossley (mathematician)|John Crossley]].<ref name="mathgene"/><ref name="aczelphd">{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|first=Peter|last=Aczel|author-link=Peter Aczel|title=Mathematical problems in logic|publisher=University of Oxford|date=1966|url=http://www.theses.com}}{{subscription required}}</ref>

==Career and research==
After two years of visiting positions at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] and [[Rutgers University]], Aczel took a position at the [[University of Manchester]].  He has also held visiting positions at the [[University of Oslo]], [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Utrecht University]], [[Stanford University]], and  [[Indiana University Bloomington]].<ref name="peter.aczel"/> In the Spring of 2009, Aczel was a Residential Fellow at the [[Swedish Collegium for Advanced Study]] in [[Uppsala]], [[Sweden]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Fellows SCAS |url=https://www.swedishcollegium.se/fellows/former-fellows/all-former-fellows }}</ref> He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars|title=Scholars|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=14 August 2015}}</ref>

Aczel was on the [[editorial board]] of the ''[[Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ndjfl.nd.edu/|title=Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic|first=Marketing Communications: Web &#124; University of Notre|last=Dame|website=Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic}}</ref> and the Cambridge Tracts in Theoretical Computer Science, having previously served on the editorial boards of the ''[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]'' and the ''[[Annals of Pure and Applied Logic]]''.<ref name="peter.aczel"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/annals-of-pure-and-applied-logic/|title=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic|via=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref>

He died on 1 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://lists.ugent.be/wws/arc/fom/2023-08/msg00006.html | title=Fom - &#91;FOM&#93; Peter Aczel - arc }}</ref>
